EA has paused development on a mobile multiplayer Sims game in favor of moving forward with a rumored Sims 4 sequel.

EA announced a wide variety of changes and projects today, including the closure of BioWare and the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 . It also seemed to lean into recent rumors that DICE and Respawn are making a new Star Wars Battlefront game . One other big change is that EA is shelving a mobile-first multiplayer Sims project, formerly known as Project Rene and now known as Project Lotus. The game was once envisioned as the next big Sims title , but plans changed to more of a mobile spin-off once EA saw that people were still hanging on to The Sims 4.

With that game being put on the back burner, EA is shifting its focus to a Sims title that it's calling Project Evergreen. Although EA hasn't revealed what the focus of this game will be, rumors have been swirling about this project for a some time now. The game, which was rumored to be under the codename Project X, is expected to be a sequel to The Sims 4. Now, here's where it may get a bit confusing: It's not The Sims 5. It's being viewed more like The Sims 4 2.0. I know, it is unnecessarily complicated.

As covered by Sims Community , the project is reportedly targeting September 2027 as its deadline to go gold, suggesting the game would launch in fall 2027. The game will release on PC and is also expected to be optimized for portable handhelds, such as the Steam Deck. If it really is releasing next year, we will likely hear more about it at The Game Awards or sometime in the first half of 2027.

Earlier this year, the team behind The Sims hinted at a new single-player game in the franchise for PC and console, noting that half of its development team was working on The Sims 4 and its "next evolution."

Ultimately, this sounds like a win for fans who have been hoping for a new traditional entry in the franchise. The Sims 4 was released in 2014, meaning it has been 12 years since the franchise got a new game. There are a ton of updates and expansions that keep the game fresh, but building something from scratch and moving away from all the bloat could be a strong move for the future of the series.

others.title: 尽管 Infinity Ward 已官方修复，《现代战争 4》的 DMZ 玩家仍因服务器崩溃而失去战利品

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/09/mw4-dmz-ea-1791562031815.jpg
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's new extraction mode, DMZ, is experiencing server issues, causing players to lose newly earned loot.

Yesterday, Infinity Ward put its new extraction mode into early access ahead of MW4's full release on Friday. It's giving players a chance to mess around with the game's other offerings before the main course is unleashed, and while the reception has been glowing so far, there are some issues. The game's been having server crashes, casuing to players lose any loot they picked up.

Thankfully, any loot that you already extracted to the FOB and brought back into the DMZ as part of a loadout is safe, but anything you picked up during the run that you were booted from is lost. Infinity Ward claims the matter has been fixed and has confirmed what players will keep and lose.

"Players who disconnected due to this particular issue will retain the equipment they started the match with and their subsequent progression, but not the loot collected during the match," devs said in an update on Twitter/X.

📢 Call of Duty: #ModernWarfare4 | #DMZ Early Access We’re aware of an issue causing some players to disconnect from matches. We’ve deployed a potential fix and are monitoring the results. Players who disconnected due to this particular issue will retain the equipment they started the match with and their subsequent progression, but not the loot collected during the match.

Some players are still reporting problems, so your mileage may vary. Of course, it's difficult to ensure everything that a player had when they were booted is safe. If that were the case, it could theoretically be abused by players to extract valuable loot without having to actually find an extraction zone. Still, if you found something extremely rare or valuable and lost it due to technical issues, it would be extremely frustrating.

Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had similar issues when it launched last year. The PvE extraction mode encouraged players to grind for rewards, but if you died or failed to extract, you would lose everything. Unfortunately, that also applied to crashes during the game's first few days. This was eventually fixed, but it was an agonizing first impression for anyone who spent hours grinding the game, only for it to be undone by something out of your control.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's full release will hit on October 23. The game's acclaimed campaign and DMZ modes are available to play now for owners of the title.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/burger-shot-1792623074820.jpg
One of the most iconic fast food restaurants from the GTA universe is becoming real ahead of GTA 6's release.

Rockstar Games' takeover of Miami is continuing to expand with a real-life version of Burger Shot, a famous fast-food restaurant in the GTA franchise. A fan on X shared the first images and info about the burger joint with GTA fan accounts, noting that it would be available at the Kaseya Center, which is the arena where the Miami Heat play.

It's unclear if the actual menu will be themed after the in-game restaurant, but it's sort of hard to imagine it will be. In GTA, Burger Shot pokes fun at fast food joints like McDonald's and Burger King for their extremely unhealthy meals. In the game, Burger Shot has menu items like "The Heartstopper," which features seven patties stacked high between a variety of toppings.

Miami's Kaseya Center has rebranded its burger restaurant as Burger Shot with Macca & Friends and Vice City posters also appearing inside the venue as part of #GTAVI's marketing campaign. Via @GTAVI_Countdown / @nvtnp_ https://t.co/FP3ly6kNen

It seems more likely that this is all purely decorative, but still, it's a fun touch. Additionally, leaks have indicated that Rockstar is also planning to sell some of the beer brands available in GTA 6 at bars in Miami. It's unclear if they will be available in retail stores or online for fans outside of Florida.

Rockstar Games has other ambitious plans for the Kaseya Center, including an unprecdented regular season game where the Miami Heat will turn into the Vice City heat for one night on November 18. The team will be given new jerseys and play on a GTA 6-themed court.

Rockstar has spent the last few weeks preparing for launch in Miami with extravagant marketing, which includes a $975,000 neon sign on top of the Kaseya Center that reads "Welcome to Vice City." Fans also recently spotted flashy GTA-branded sports cars driving around Miami . The cars were seen with camera crews, suggesting some kind of live-action advertising is happening for GTA 6.
We're officially less than a month away from launch, as GTA 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC version is also rumored to release early next year.

items.title: 迄今为止《使命召唤：现代战争 4 DMZ》评测
items.summary: This bigger and better version of DMZ makes a great first impression.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/codwf4dmz-blogroll-1792622752717.jpg
This is a standalone review that covers only Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode. You can find our campaign review here , with multiplayer impressions to follow after launch.

Extraction shooters feel a little like a modern trend, with some heavy hitters like Marathon and Arc Raiders shaking the table within the last year or so, but they’ve been a growing experiment in the shooter space for the past decade or so. Call of Duty dabbled in it with the original DMZ back in 2022 (you could argue they were late to the party then), and its return in 2026 is timely. But with so much high quality competition on the market, is it welcome? I’ve only dipped my toe in since its “pay to play on time” launch on Tuesday – about five or so hours of vehicle hijacking, SAM site hacking, and target elimination on my docket so far – but this bigger, better DMZ makes a great first impression.

The PvPvE dynamic of extraction shooters often lives and dies by how well the mission and level design encourages you to explore, rewards you for overcoming challenges, and guides you to interact with others in order to keep those spoils. The fictional Korean Hajin region your exploits take place in is well suited for this. Its dense pockets of urban development – a village in the north, the dangerous main city in the east, an isolated prison out west – are separated by rocky forests concealing all sorts of militarized checkpoints and other points of interest hiding loot to shove into your pockets. Parts of it look a little samey, the consequence of modern urban development where (at least from the outside) most buildings look the same, especially compared to some of DMZ’s big sci-fi competition that go above and beyond to look striking at first glance.

The map is so big that you could spend the entirety of your approximately half-hour runs in only a fraction of it. Battle Royales (like CoD’s own Warzone) move players around by having an encroaching death cloud forcing everyone into a smaller and smaller area. DMZ instead entices squads to adventure with its Dynamic Operations.

Dynamic Ops are spontaneous missions that appear as you travel across the battlefield which come in lots of forms, from securing a package to blowing up a target to escorting a VIP. Many of them are multi-stage affairs that have your fireteam moving from point to point as NPC enemies ramp up a more coordinated defense against you. These all get rewarded by supply drops that grant you loot, the value of which escalates based on how many of them you're successfully completing. I prefer this sort of objective chasing to the more standard task lists in other games like this (which also exist here, in fairness) because it makes for more engaging individual runs. I’ll prepare the best I can beforehand, but can’t be ready for every possible string of operations once I deploy.

There are many actions and events, like aforementioned supply drops, that are broadcast to everyone within earshot, hypothetically to tempt other players to be nosy (and potentially belligerent), but my skirmishes with others have been pretty limited so far. It’s still technically the early access period, so a wave of operators is set to crash against me in the coming days, but I found that most people have opted to mind their own business. It would be a mistake to confuse this passivity with pacifism though – this isn’t the Arc Raiders playerbase, which spent many of the opening months of that game more interested in helping than hurting. Whenever another player was in eye or earshot, it was assumed that a fire fight was to follow. It’s just unclear at this point how much of that was motivated by them wanting what I had versus just coincidentally being in the same place at the same time.

Hajin is also a pretty lively place. Enemy patrols speed down roadways, sometimes as lone jeeps and other times in large caravans. Helicopters and drones streak across the skies looking for interlopers like me, or occasionally other NPCs from rival factions tearing the map apart. A train runs on a schedule, and you can absolutely hitch a ride on it to get from place to place. Squads of enemies could be posted up anywhere. Weird exploding robot dogs can sniff you out as you slink from building to building. There was always at least a base level of tension with every step I took or round I let off, because there was just enough going on around me that any push I made could be the one that knocks over the house of cards I was hiding behind.

Clashes with the NPC denizens of the DMZ start pretty tame, but ramp up as you and your squad make yourself more notorious by killing enemies and completing objectives. As enemy units start to don armor, pull up in more durable vehicles, and use higher grade weaponry to take you down, fire fights can get desperate quickly. There's an instinct for people in pick-up groups to run out on their own, potentially to get first dibs on loot perhaps, and they almost always regret it – it doesn’t take much for enemies to get the drop on you, as you are only where you are and they are potentially anywhere and everywhere else.

Call of Duty’s top tier military shooter gunplay, toeing the line between the lethality of simulations and the snappy speed of arcadey romps, feels at home in DMZ as well. All of the new tweaks, like the way your weapons interact with your surroundings or movement adjustments, feel like it had roaming gunfights in an open world in mind. Being able to cancel out of mantles so you aren’t stuck in an animation when you least want to be feels like the kind of quality of life inclusion that Warzone demonstrated was needed for a long time. That said, the smattering of guns lack much in the way of real identities outside of the normal archetypal framings that have existed in gaming forever (shotgun, assault rifle, sniper, etc.).

You can also drop into story missions, which are quest chains that include more structure, resembling the campaign missions without the more cinematic story elements. These were pretty rowdy and unique, like an escort mission where our squad had to wheel an injured general out of hospital, bed and all, while enduring swarms of enemy combatants. There's a finite number of these and the possible rewards are more limited, with less incentive to explore the places around you and no enemy players to pirate or evade. But they serve as a great tasting platter of the pace Dynamic Ops keep and a good tour of the various locations you'll need to get familiar with on the map.

In between missions, you tend to all of your gear and progression from the safety of your FOB. Weapons, crafting ingredients, and consumables that you procure out in the field can be sorted through here, all of it put at risk when you equip it and redeploy. When you unlock the 3D printer and gunsmith areas, crafting new toys and upgrading weapons becomes the main way you spend your plunder to enhance your chances in Hajin. The value proposition of spending in-game money on upgrades is still hard to parse for me this early on. You can easily blow tens of thousands of won to trick out a weapon, but there hasn't been an obvious benefit to doing so that outweighs the risk of throwing all of that hard earned money down the drain if you die while using it. That’s the kind of knowledge that only comes with reps, I imagine.

items.title: 机械迷城 AI 致敬警察遭工作室鞭打：“这看起来很恶心，与我们或我们的手艺无关”
items.summary: Three cheers for the slop intolerant.

content.v: On October 20, the CEO for "AI storytelling" company Nura Studios posted a now-deleted tribute to Amanita Design's 2009 cult classic Machinarium. I saw a glimpse of the video while it was still live and it was undeniably AI generated, but that probably goes without saying given its provenance.

It wasn't good, but then: Amanita Design is one of the most visually distinctive studios in the world. The Czech-based team is also among the most assertive, if its response to Nura Studios' video is anything to go by.

"The audacity to feed Machinarium assets to AI, make AI slop animations, and call it a love letter…," the studio tweeted of the AI tribute. "Love letters are supposed to be handwritten. This looks disgusting and has nothing to do with us or our craft."

Ouch. Under these circumstances a studio would normally politely ignore the clumsy advances of a mob like Nura Studios, whose mission is "to empower creators with a human-led AI platform to bring high-quality stories to life", and whose website looks like this:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/fnYAu3QZaHxVQvx45ofhNA-1920-80.png
So it's gratifying to see Amanita push back.

Nura Studios CEO Sylvio Drouin did show remorse. "We are so sorry for the post we did," Drouin tweeted. "We thought it was an homage to your amazing work and I already deleted the posts, again please accept our sincere apologies."
Amanita Design has yet to publicly accept the apology. Its next game, Machinarium 2 , was announced earlier this month.

content.v: 近日在2026柏林GTC大会上，英伟达CEO黄仁勋提出新观点：面向AI的数据中心GPU，有效经济使用寿命可达8年甚至更久。传统行业认知里，AI加速卡的更新折旧周期大约是4年。黄仁勋表示，CUDA持续软件优化、AI推理业务需求上涨，能拉长硬件的实际使用价值。即便芯片硬件本身没有变化，通过软件更新，老GPU依旧可以持续产出商业收益，不应该快速淘汰报废。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792620169_946812_jpg_r.jpg
而马斯克在财报电话会议也表达了相近但角度不同的看法，他认为随着大模型、软件算法不断迭代，老旧GPU可以释放出更高的“每瓦智能(intelligence‑per‑watt)”。意思是同一套旧硬件，搭配更新更好的AI模型，单位功耗可以产出更多有效的AI智能输出。他举例H100这类老加速卡，现在的租赁价格甚至高于刚上市阶段，算力需求推高了旧硬件的商业价值。
注意，二者讨论对象均为数据中心AI计算GPU，并非消费级游戏显卡。不代表硬件物理不会老化，谈论的是商业、经济层面的可用周期。GPU依旧会发生折旧，只是贬值速度比市场此前预估更慢。硬件规格固定，但软件与模型优化可以持续挖掘旧硬件的算力潜力。
华尔街部分分析师对此持保留态度，警告一旦算力供给过剩，老旧GPU的租赁价值会快速下滑。

items.title: CD Projekt 老板向 BioWare 致敬，感谢 BioWare 在 20 年前帮助将《巫师》变为现实：“BioWare 已成为 CDPR 历史的重要组成部分”
items.summary: BioWare let CD Projekt use the Aurora Engine for its breakout RPG, and then helped them show it off at E3.

content.v: BioWare was a legendary studio, and its shocking closure today has inspired numerous tributes from fans and fellow game developers alike. One of the most notable came from CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski, who credited the studio for the big role it played in bringing The Witcher to life.

It's hard to overstate the impact BioWare had on computer RPGs, from effectively resurrecting the genre in the 1990s with Baldur's Gate through the creation of Neverwinter Nights, Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, and Mass Effect. But less well known, outside of RPG fan circles at least, is that its influence goes far beyond that. CD Projekt, which is arguably the contemporary equivalent of BioWare, literally got started with BioWare games.

The relationship began when CD Projekt approached BioWare and Interplay about localizing Baldur's Gate for Poland; it got the gig, and the Polish release became a major hit. A subsequent deal to localize Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance fell apart when Interplay did, but CD Projekt's relationship with BioWare held firm.

"Bioware has been a massive part of CDPR history," Nowakowski wrote on X. "We befriended them when localizing and selling Baldur’s Gate games in Poland, Czech, and Slovakia. And later they were great help when lending us their engine for Witcher 1, sharing their wisdom and even giving us a spot at their booth at E3."

Bioware has been a massive part of CDPR history. We befriended them when localizing and selling Baldur’s Gate games in Poland, Czech, and Slovakia. And later they were great help when lending us their engine for Witcher 1, sharing their wisdom and even giving us a spot at their booth at E3. I had a pleasure to visit them a few times in Edmonton and also host them in our Warsaw office. Very sad for the people affected, but also sad to see a legendary brand go down. Not a great day in the games industry. October 21, 2026

That was the Aurora Engine, BioWare's followup to the Infinity Engine, and was used for Neverwinter Nights, Knights of the Old Republic, Jade Empire, and as Nowakowski said, The Witcher, the RPG that introduced CD Projekt to the world and market the beginning of its journey to game industry powerhouse. In a 2014 interview with Polygon , CD Projekt co-founder Marcin Iwinski talked about the studio's early days working with BioWare and Interplay, and how it moved quickly to work on The Witcher after that Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance fell through: "It all started, in a way, with Baldur's Gate."

And BioWare did in fact share space with CD Projekt at E3, giving the studio a chance to show its new RPG to the world: Ryszard Chojnowski, a translator and localizer whose credits include both The Witcher and Baldur's Gate 2, shared a pair of photos showing CD Projekt's corner of BioWare's booth at E3 2004:

A tu jeszcze jedno wspomnienie.m z BioWare. Rok 2004 i po raz pierwszy pokazujemy Wiedźmina na ich stoisku. Mamy oddzielone kotarą miejsce z komputerem, na którym działa jako tako demo na silniku Aurora https://t.co/SH8FKQF9zu October 21, 2026

Nowakowski concluded, "I had a pleasure to visit them a few times in Edmonton and also host them in our Warsaw office. Very sad for the people affected, but also sad to see a legendary brand go down. Not a great day in the games industry."
Not a great day indeed.

items.title: 《现代战争 4》玩家宣布 DMZ 福利“破碎”，可让你在完全死亡后自我复活
items.summary: Some hate that you can't know an enemy's truly dead in DMZ.

content.v: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's big extraction mode DMZ has been out for one day, so it's a bit early to make sweeping declarations about balance, but even I'm raising an eyebrow at an operator trait that the internet is already calling broken.
That's "broken" in the "so overpowered it shouldn't exist" way, not the "literally doesn't work way," though when you see Possum in action, it does give the impression of a bug.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Ls3VyDL9Kqj43oXratbfod-1920-80.jpg

As someone who's been around the extraction shooter block, it's a very powerful trump card. It doesn't take that long to get, either: If you beeline straight to it on the Warfighter skill tree, you can do it in a handful of matches.

To be clear, this is not the same as reviving yourself during the DBNO (down but not out) state, which anyone can do from level 1: Possum means you can be a cold, dead, lootable body, and then suddenly spring back to life.

I'm not surprised folks are panicky about the prospect of playing around lobbies full of Possum players. There's already one clip circulating (per xFleXy_ on X) of someone fully killing a player, turning their back to fight other nearby enemies, then getting shot in the back by the guy they just killed.
Umm I kill & finish the guy in the white skin and then he suddenly pops up and kills me??? @InfinityWard @CallofDutyCM https://t.co/XFrgD6MRCI October 20, 2026

That's the nightmare scenario, though the perk has drawbacks that xFleXy could've exploited if they'd known Possum existed. The self-revive isn't quick, and once it's done they still have to pick themselves up from DBNO with a tourniquet. If the killer is paying attention when that first step happens, they can easily end them for good before they stand back up.

I reckon Infinity Ward didn't envision folks using the perk to instantly turn the table on a lost fight. Per the name, you're likely meant to sit still, play dead, then self-revive after your corpse has been picked clean and the killers have moved on. You lose some stuff, but you escape with your operator (which can be expensive to replace). Call of Duty YouTuber JGOD demonstrated this use case in his own video.
1st time using the Possum Trait in DMZ🟢Waited 3 minutes for the players to move on🟢They dropped a 2 plate while looting my Free Kit🟢Then Exfilled https://t.co/SHFgd2gJv1 October 21, 2026

In those terms, a trait like Possum is a great fit for DMZ, which is designed not to be as punishing as other extraction shooters . The problem is its execution: Players who just won a fight should not always have to worry that their victim is going to stand back up and kill them. Maybe using Possum should make more noise in the moment, or require a long wait (like 5 to 10 minutes) to use. Infinity Ward needs to underline how bad of an idea it is to use while enemies are around, or in lieu of that, players need a way to burn bodies .

"Burn bodies," in this context, refers to Hunt: Showdown, the other extraction shooter with this exact ability. That game's Possum, called Necromancer, works the same way, except that others have the option to set your corpse on fire and wait for a sound cue that confirms "this guy ain't getting up." It's a great bit of balance, because it puts the onus on the killer to already have a molotov cocktail on-hand, look for another way to start a fire, or leave your corpse and accept you may come back. Sometimes Necromancer saves your bacon, sometimes not.
Whatever the eventual solution is, I expect Infinity Ward to react soon.

content.v: 《GTA3》问世25周年之际，一篇回顾文章重新审视了它的行业影响。文章认为，真正留下深远影响的并非暴力争议，而是三维开放世界带来的玩家自由、成熟叙事与创作表达。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792618124_600390_jpg_r.jpg
这款作品在2001年重新点燃了有关电子游戏暴力、犯罪行为及未成年人影响的公共争论。不过，回顾文章认为，这些争议并不是它最重要的历史遗产。系列前两作采用俯视角2D形式，第三作则以三维自由城显著提升了现实感和沉浸感。
玩家可以暂时放下主线，自行选择路线并探索城市，还能观察行人、商店、警察和急救人员如何应对城市中的事件。文章强调，《GTA3》并非最早采用开放世界或城市开放世界设计的游戏，但它推动了这类设计的普及与完善，也让城市本身成为与 剧情 同样重要的吸引力。
游戏还借犯罪世界、道德复杂的角色、黑色幽默、虚构广告和电台节目，对消费主义、政治观念及社会规范展开讽刺，挑战了“电子游戏只属于儿童”的看法。文章最终将其深远创新归结为扩大玩家自由、成熟叙事和创作表达的边界，并为此后数十年的开发者提供设计参照。

content.v: 近日《猛鬼追魂：复苏》叙事总监Antony De Fault向外媒IGN透露，开发团队曾设下一个“非正式目标”：让游戏在世界上至少一个地区遭到禁售、拒绝评级或限制，以此判断团队是否真正呈现了《猛鬼追魂》系列应有的极端尺度。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792618068_400392_jpg_r.jpg
Saber Interactive希望内容的直白程度能够匹配系列电影以及恐怖作家克莱夫·巴克的原著小说《地狱之心》。据悉，《猛鬼追魂：复苏》包含男女正面全裸、自残、重度 血腥 和强烈性行为等内容。
De Fault强调，团队并不满足于让玩家旁观禁忌场面，还希望玩家在第一人称视角下主动参与极端暴力、性互动及其他令人不适的行为，同时仍保留传统 生存 恐怖机制。团队也为避免越过评级门槛做过细微调整：一段涉及角色自慰的场景通过房间布局阻止玩家看到正面画面。
De Fault称如果直接展示生殖器，很可能导致评级突破门槛，使作品无法在多数地区销售。游戏在多数国家以未删减形式推出，并获得当地最高年龄等级。印尼游戏评级系统则给予RC，即拒绝分级，实际上令其无法在当地销售，也使团队达成了上述非正式目标。

content.v: 《使命召唤：现代 战争 4》PC版所有在线模式均要求启用TPM 2.0和安全启动，准备首发游玩多人模式或DMZ的玩家还需检查TPM固件版本。即使系统显示两项功能已经开启，Intel平台的PTT或AMD平台的fTPM版本不兼容时，部分电脑仍需更新BIOS。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792615905_295886_jpg_r.jpg
目前列出的不兼容版本包括Intel平台的302.1.2.X和303.1.2.X，以及AMD平台的3.X.0.X。玩家可以按Win+R打开运行窗口，输入“tpm.msc”，随后在“TPM制造商信息”中查看当前版本。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792615906_206347_jpg_r.jpg
该问题并不局限于非常老旧的处理器。两台分别采用Intel Core i5-12400KF和AMD Ryzen 5 5800X的电脑也遇到了版本不兼容，不过它们的BIOS均已多年没有更新。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792615907_214590_jpg_r.jpg
需要升级的玩家应前往主板制造商网站，下载与具体型号对应的最新稳定版BIOS，并按照主板规定的流程操作。由于升级通常会重置设置，完成后还要重新确认安全启动、TPM、PTT或fTPM已经启用。
玩家还应检查内存XMP或EXPO配置、风扇曲线、首选启动盘和Resizable BAR等设置是否发生变化。相关要求将通过安全启动和TPM验证固件及启动过程，以协助在线模式抵御作弊或恶意软件。

content.v: 近日EA官方公布大规模内部重组计划，BioWare(生软)正式关闭，处于早期开发阶段的全新《质量效应》项目直接取消。同时砍掉代号“莲花(Project Lotus)”的《模拟人生》新作，全公司裁员约400人，占总员工数3%，其中约50人来自BioWare埃德蒙顿工作室。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792615779_629517.jpg
BioWare是定义现代角色扮演游戏品类的传奇工作室，打造了《博德之门》《质量效应》《龙腾世纪》系列。EA官方表示：“BioWare是塑造RPG行业的传奇工作室，做出这个决定我们绝非轻率为之”。BioWare关闭前仅剩不到百名员工，主力投入下一代《质量效应》前期研发，项目尚未进入实质制作阶段就宣告终止。
EA于今年8月完成550亿美元杠杆收购转为私有企业，背负高额债务，管理层要求削减研发开支，计划最高压缩7亿美元成本。《龙腾世纪：影障守护者》商业销量不及预期，也加速了本次业务调整。
本次重组项目变动一览
BioWare & 质量效应
BioWare永久关闭，新《质量效应》早期项目彻底取消。《质量效应》《龙腾世纪》IP版权依旧归EA所有，但暂无重启新作、出售IP的消息。亚马逊《质量效应》电视剧项目命运尚未明朗。BioWare 官方发布告别声明：我们不只是一间工作室，是创作者与玩家共同的家园，现阶段优先妥善安置被裁员工。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792615861_475163.jpg
模拟人生系列
代号Project Lotus新作直接取消。代号Project Evergreen的另一款《模拟人生》项目保留，提升为优先开发项目继续推进。
其他项目变动
免费滑板游戏《skate》项目保留，但开发团队规模大幅缩减。重点加码资源：《Apex英雄》、EA SPORTS体育产品线、《星球大战：绝地》续作、漫威《钢铁侠》新作。《战地》系列继续开发，Respawn与DICE将合作新项目，传闻为《星球大战：前线3》。《搏击之夜》格斗系列开启前期筹备，还有一款全新开放世界美式橄榄球游戏立项。
BioWare关闭消息放出后，大量粉丝、业内开发者发文悼念这间传奇工作室。CDPR高管公开表示惋惜，早年BioWare曾经向CDPR借出游戏引擎，助力初代《巫师》的开发。前BioWare编剧 Patrick Weekes发表猜测，新控股方的价值取向，或许也是促使EA砍掉BioWare的潜在因素。

content.v: Xbox新任首席执行官阿莎・夏尔马，正计划对Xbox Game Pass订阅服务开展一次重大改版，改革力度超过此前已经落地的部分调整，例如《使命召唤》新作不再保证首发入库等变动。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261022/1792615246_159921_jpg_r.jpg
根据《财富》获取的内部消息，微软计划改造Game Pass现有模式，未来玩家可以单点自选订阅功能(点菜式订阅)。改革后服务依旧保留分级框架，云游戏、多人联机、主机独占游戏库等内容，都会作为可选附加组件，在基础套餐之上按需选购。
简单来说：玩家不再必须购买全套捆绑大包，只需要为自己实际用到的功能付费。只玩单机的用户可以不买联机权限，只玩云串流的玩家可以只选购云游戏模块。
早先就有传闻称，微软在研究带广告的低价档位，同时讨论是否要取消第一方游戏首日加入XGP的政策，还规划了家庭套餐等多项改动。今年4月有消息透露，微软在研发“自选组件” 式Game Pass，与本次报道内容相吻合。
夏尔马本人曾公开表态，希望把Game Pass进化成一套更加灵活的系统。她也坦言，过去押注Game Pass的激进策略并没有拿到预期回报，因此启动大刀阔斧的业务调整也就不难理解。此前团队已经做出多项改动，包括把新作《使命召唤》移出XGP首发阵容、调整部分档位售价等。
目前Xbox整体业务大环境是内部不同团队目标互相冲突，订阅业务在带来持续收入的同时，也挤压了买断制游戏的销量。Xbox部门整体利润率偏低，公司还规划多轮裁员;下一代主机Project Helix、Xbox掌机硬件项目也在同步推进。

items.title: 《质量效应 5》原定会在《仙女座》之后拯救该系列，但现在我们永远不会实现了
items.summary: I'm the sort of person that just replays my favorite games whenever there's a big gap between releases. And a

content.v: https://assets1.ignimgs.com/2012/11/07/omegan7day-5jpg-5a7c69.jpg
This is an IGN opinion piece by Jackie Thomas, who has been playing and replaying Mass Effect for nearly 20 years now.

I'm the sort of person who replays my favorite games whenever there's a big gap between releases. And those favorites usually end up being from the Mass Effect series, whether it's just the first game or a run through the entire original trilogy. So, for me, a Mass Effect 5 that captured the magic of the first three games has been something I've been looking forward to since before it was even announced in 2021. Now, that game will never exist, thanks to EA closing down BioWare . And that f**king sucks.

When Mass Effect came out in 2007, I stood in line to get it on release night, and I played it incessently until I finished absolutely everything in it. I did the same thing when the second and third games came out, except I also played the previous games again ahead of time so everything would be fresh in my mind.

Ever since Mass Effect 3 came out, I've replayed the original games maybe a dozen times. I don't even drastically change the way I play Mass Effect each time I play it. Even after nearly 20 years of experiencing the original game, I still play an Adept every time, because pistols are OP and bionics are cool. And I still ultimately do a paragon playthrough, even when I tell myself that I'm going to be bad and play renegade. Mass Effect has felt like home to me for years, and it became my ultimate comfort game.

But eventually, Mass Effect Andromeda came out, and even though I tried to power through it, I ultimately gave up after a deluge of bugs and weird writing turned me off. I still haven't gone back and finished that game, but I still find myself downloading and playing Mass Effect when I run out of other games to play. Hell, with the amount of times I've played the first game, I can probably navigate most of its empty optional planets with my eyes closed. After today's news, I might just download it and play it again in solidarity.

You'd think that after getting burned on Mass Effect Andromeda, I would've learned my lesson. But in the years since Bioware teased what should have the fifth Mass Effect game, I let myself hope that it would redeem the series once again and land in that annual ME replay rotation.

And I know that after Anthem , and Dragon Age: The Veilguard's weird shift to a straight-up action game, I didn't have much of a reason to believe that Mass Effect 5 would have been this magical return to form. But I think what's hitting me the hardest about BioWare's closure is that we'll never know whether or not Mass Effect 5 would have been good.

The truth is, we didn't know much about the next Mass Effect game at all. Hell, I don't even know if it would have been called Mass Effect 5, but that's just easier to say than 'the next Mass Effect game' over and over again. Ever since it was announced, BioWare had been pretty quiet about the project, only really speaking up to reassure fans that it was still in development. And look how that turned out.

But some of the things that popped up about the game over the years did look pretty cool. Bioware showed off some concept art late last year, showing a Krogan civil war with a properly grizzled Krogan leading a whole squad of the grumpy lizards in a fight. I want to play that game.

Likewise, in one of the only teasers we ever got , the camera zooms through the galaxy, past what looks like the ruins of the Citadel, until it finally shows an older Asari climbing up some snowy ruins. And we don't see her full face, but even from the side, it sure looked like Liara. And, again, I'd love to revisit her character after she fully becomes an Asari Matriarch. But again, that game will never exist.

But there is at least hope that some games that are at least similar to Mass Effect are on the horizon. Just last year, Mass Effect director Casey Hudson's new studio announced Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic . I'm a huge Star Wars fan, so when that game comes eventually comes out, I'm sure I'll burrow my way into it like a tick and not come out for a week. But, just like Mass Effect 5, there's not a lot we know about Fate of the Old Republic quite yet. But at least Hudson has come out and said that it won't take until 2030 to release, so maybe we'll get it in 2029.

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn is another one that I've had my eye on, and while I haven't really watched the show or read the books (even though both are on my list), I know that universe has a lot of potential for a Mass-Effect-Like. Then, there's Exodus , which is made by Wizards of the Coast of all companies, and has Mass Effect alumni working on it. The art style even makes it look like a Mass Effect game. Luckily, both of these titles seem like they're on track to actually come out next year, but only time will tell there.

As much as I'm earnestly looking forward to all three of those games, they're simply not Mass Effect. The aesthetics are there, the writing should be there, and it looks like the gameplay for Exodus at least is going to be quite good. And Fate of the Old Republic is a Star Wars game, and my love of Star Wars is what led me to play Mass Effect in the first place.

But no matter how good they end up being, I don't know if it's going to be as relaxing as hunting down all of the Keepers in the Citadel, and I probably won't be fighting a giant Reaper skeleton inside of a black hole. I am at least thankful that no matter how controversial Mass Effect 3's ending was, it was at least an ending . I would have loved another chapter and a chance to see whatever Bioware was cooking up with Mass Effect 5. But, at least I'll always have those first three games, and no amount of EA's mismanagement is going to take that away from me.

items.title: Steam 上 100 款最常玩的游戏列表中的 Next Fest 演示是一款商店模拟游戏，这让我感到非常高兴
items.summary: (Don't worry, you don't need to be a sim geek to dig it.)

content.v: As the sicko cartoon goes: "YES… HA HA HA… YES! " That's how I feel while peering at Steam's 100 most-played games list and spotting the Next Fest demo for shopkeeping sim Probably Stolen.

A singleplayer game about sitting behind a desk and managing inventory doing that well among the other 8,000+ demos that have arrived for Next Fest? So well it's actually charting with 34,230 concurrent players?
YES!

I played the demo back in September and loved it because it made me feel like I was running a corner store in Dredd or Cyberpunk 2077 . You sit behind the counter of a grimy little shop on a space station and sell everything from food and beverages to weapons and cybernetic implants to a collection of interesting, unusual, and occasionally suspicious customers.

There's a bit of Fallout to it, as well: at night you can go and scavenge scrap and junk from trashpiles in hopes of adding something valuable to your inventory. You can do some crafting, too, smelting metals into ingots once you've got the gear for it, and this is the grim future so you can also start a rat farm and sell off the meat.

You can shop at other specialty vendors to acquire hard-to-find items to use or sell yourself, and there's even a bit of Papers, Please with the moral dilemmas you'll face: there's an underground movement fighting against the cyber-dystopia you can help or hinder, depending on if you want to turn a revolutionary in for a tidy bounty or keep your mouth shut if you spot someone on the cops' most-wanted list.

And don't worry, you don't need to be a huge sim geek to enjoy running the shop in Probably Stolen. The sim does go enjoyably deep, though: you can use a magnifying glass (Strange Horticulture style) to examine items for signs of counterfeiting, and even sell those counterfeit goods yourself to rich dummies who wouldn't know a legitimate cyber implant from a fake.

In other words, I'm pumped to see Probably Stolen getting so many players during Steam Next Fest, and you should become one of those players if you aren't already. There's not much longer to wait for the full game, either: Probably Stolen launches next week on October 28.

content.v: In anticipation of the full launch of World of Warcraft: Forever next month, Blizzard is throwing the gates wide open on the throwback MMO to stress test the servers.

Anyone with a World of Warcraft account will be able to play the 'WoW: Forever - Stress Test" client in the Battle.net launcher later today. You don't need an active subscription, nor do you need to have purchased any of the WoW: Forever special editions. All you need is some patience for what could be a bumpy few hours as people pile in.

The regular beta servers will be offline until the stress test is over, which means anyone who can't go that long without a hit of WoW: Forever will likely show up. I wouldn't be surprised if some Blizzard folks drop in with some surprises of their own, like spawning world bosses or something in the last hour or so (this happened during a recent PvP tournament).

Everyone will start fresh on the stress test server, so you won't have time to do much but the first couple of leveling zones. You will get a taste of what to expect on launch day: Crowds of players wandering around like ants, and quest enemies dying before you can even click on them. Get ready to fight for your XP.
Here are all the times for the WoW: Forever stress test:
Once everything wraps up, Blizzard is going to flip the switch back on for the regular beta servers until Friday.

I'm crossing my fingers that this stress test actually helps with stability on launch day. There will almost certainly be long queue times, but having to start and stop as servers go haywire will ruin any chance of actually enjoying the game that day. We already witnessed this with the launch of the beta , and that was only the people who paid for the game. On November 4, when WoW: Forever properly goes live, anyone out there with a subscription will be lining up.

items.summary: Follow three simple steps, and you can save $11 off Grand Theft Auto 6, today only.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/17/gta-6-soundtrack-1789662158949.jpg

We’re less than a month out from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. If you haven’t yet placed your preorder, here’s a good reason to do so: you can (indirectly) save $11 on a PS5 copy or $10 on an Xbox copy right now. You just have to follow a simple three-step process to do so. Let’s take a look.

The deal starts with buying a digital gift card from Newegg. Today only, you can get a $100 PlayStation Store gift card on sale for $89 , or a $100 Xbox gift card on sale for $90 . As luck would have it, $100 is how much the ultimate edition of Grand Theft Auto VI costs.
Step 1: Buy a Discounted Gift Card at Newegg

Make sure you use the promo codes, or you won't get the discount on the gift card, making this all for naught. A little while after you successfully place your order, you'll receive an email with a redeemable code for your digital gift card.
Step 2: Redeem the Gift Card
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/screenshot-2026-10-21-at-2-38-09-pm-1792607989270.png

Regardless of which digital storefront you're using to buy GTA 6, use the appropriate link above and sign into your account. Then click your avatar in the upper right of the page and select "Redeem Code" from the dropdown menu. Paste the code in there, hit enter, and now you should have $100 in your digital wallet.
Step 3: Buy GTA 6

The standard edition gets you the game, along with the Vintage Vice City Pack, and one month of GTA+. The Ultimate edition includes everything that comes in the standard edition, plus “an exclusive collection of premium vehicles, weapons, apparel, and action threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia’s story.”

When preorders first went live, we saw reports that way more people were buying the ultimate edition than the standard edition. That makes sense, as early preorders would mostly be made by the biggest fans, who would be the most likely to splurge on the ultimate edition. You can check out our full GTA 6 preorder guide for more info.

This isn’t the first time this type of deal has popped up while GTA 6 has been available for preorder. Roughly every week or two, Newegg offers similar discounts on PlayStation Store and Xbox Store gift cards. You always have to enter a promo code, and the deals always last just one day. So if you miss out this time, you’ll probably have another shot or two before the official GTA 6 release date.

If you do preorder Grand Theft Auto 6, you’ll be able to preload the game onto your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S starting on November 12. That’s a week prior to the game’s release. Then, once launch day rolls around, you’ll already have the game on your console and ready to go when start time arrives.
As a reminder: at launch, you’ll only have access to the GTA 6 campaign. Rockstar hasn’t announced when GTA Online will be available, so keep it locked on IGN for further information on that front.

items.summary: The changes predicted when Saudi Arabia's PIF bought Electronic Arts are coming true.

content.v: Following the shocking closure of legendary RPG studio BioWare , Electronic Arts has posted a lengthy missive laying out its plans for " EA's next chapter ," which sounds very much like cuts almost across the board.

I'll spare you the corporate gobbledygook about challenging assumptions, confronting assumptions , and imagining new possibilities , and cut straight to the chase: The plan is to do fewer things with fewer people focusing on its biggest franchises. What that works out to practically:

Of course, there's also a gross little nod to BioWare and the end of Mass Effect: "As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly."

The message doesn't specifically reference the layoff of around 400 employees at Electronic Arts reported by Bloomberg , but it does say some of the changes announced today "are difficult, especially for the people and teams across the company who are directly affected," which is the sort of mealy-mouthed guffola put out by C-suites when they don't want to say with clarity that they just hacked out a significant chunk of their workforce.

One other thing I find interesting about this announcement: It's attributed to Cam and David, who I assume are Cam Weber and David Tinson , recently installed near the top of EA as president and chief studios officer, and president and chief operating officer. The name of Andrew Wilson, Electronic Arts CEO, is rather notably absent. Make of that what you will—but for the record, EA confirmed that Wilson is still the chief executive.

The post is short on detail, but the broad gist of the whole thing—cuts and concentration—aren't entirely surprising given the company's recent acquisition by Saudi Arabia, which saddled it with $20 billion in debt and owners not known for their liberal mindset . Plans for massive cuts were reported in early August, and a possible merger with Saudi-owned Savvy Games Group has also been rumored . But former BioWare lead writer Patrick Weekes made the call more than a year ago, when the EA acquisition first happened, predicting that "guns and football" games would be fine , but "gay stuff" would be out.

items.title: EA Cancels New Mass Effect, Pauses New Sims Game, And All The Other Big EA News That Just Happened
items.summary: When EA was acquired by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, many expected major changes at the gaming compa

content.v: When EA was acquired by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, many expected major changes at the gaming company, including layoffs and game cancellations, among other shakeups. Now, those have begun, with EA on October 21 confirming a series of significant changes impacting the people and teams that worked on many storied franchises.
EA also teased some of what's to come in the future, including a joint project between Respawn and DICE. Here's a rundown of all the big EA news today.
Layoffs

EA said in a statement that it made the "difficult" choice to lay off staff, and Bloomberg reported that the cuts will impact about 400 people. Affected staffers will be treated with "care and respect," EA said, and some impacted employees may have a chance to get a different job within EA. Alongside the BioWare closure noted below, staff at Ripple Effect (Battlefield), Maxis (The Sims), and Full Circle (Skate) have been impacted, as noted by Vertical Slice .
BioWare closes and new Mass Effect axed

BioWare, the esteemed Canadian developer founded 30+ years ago, is shutting down. The studio employed fewer than 100 people, Bloomberg reported, and the team was working on the next Mass Effect. That game is now canceled.
"BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly," EA said.

Developers at BioWare had feared their jobs were at risk after PIF announced that it would buy EA. BioWare is known, in part, for making pro-diversity games featuring inclusive storytelling and characters.

Longtime BioWare writer Patrick Weekes, who was laid off in 2025, speculated that EA’s new owners, including the PIF, might want to avoid “gay stuff” and politics that the PIF’s leadership does not agree with.
There has been an outpouring of support and thoughtful messages about BioWare in the wake of the news, from fans and industry professionals alike.

CD Projekt's Michal Nowakowski said his company first got to know BioWare when the studio did the work to localize Baldur's Gate games in Europe. Later, BioWare lent its game engine to CD Projekt for the first Witcher game.
"Very sad for the people affected, but also sad to see a legendary brand go down. Not a great day in the games industry," he said.
New The Sims game paused

Another game that's not going ahead at EA is Project Lotus, the codename for new game in The Sims franchise. Another The Sims game, codename Project Evergreen, is now the main focus for the developers working on The Sims. Exactly what this game is, however, remains a mystery, but The Sims is a juggernaut at EA and fans have been waiting for a new game for a long time.
Skate gets scaled back

EA's new Skate game, which was released in 2025, will remain online, but EA said it's "making changes to the studio," and that includes cutting staff to create a "more focused, smaller team." EA said this will help Skate have a "very clear roadmap" and one that can lead to a "healthier and more sustainable business."
EA Sports open-world football game

The EA Sports division, which is among the strongest at the company due in part to the lucrative loot boxes and microtransactions in Ultimate Team modes, continue to operate "from a position of strength," EA said. In addition to the usual annual sports games, EA said it has two new projects in the works, including a "brand-new, social-first open-world" football game in the works under the codename Project Gridiron. The other project is the next Fight Night, which is coming back after a 15-year hiatus .
Shooters

EA said Battlefield 6 was a "great success," and that the studio "learned a lot from the launch and live service." There will be future Battlefield games, as well as a new project to be collaboratively developed by Respawn and DICE. EA didn't say what this will be, but many believe it could be a new Star Wars: Battlefront, following recent rumors that DICE could make that game . Variety reported that yes, indeed, a new Battlefront game is coming. This would not be surprising at all, given DICE's two previous Battlefront games sold a combined 33 million+ copies.
As for Apex Legends, EA said it will continue to "invest heavily" in the franchise by adding new gameplay modes and "other new experiences."
Iron Man and Star Wars Jedi

While EA may have canceled its Black Panther game already, the company's other big Marvel game, Iron Man, remains in development. Additionally, the next Star Wars Jedi game is still on the way, EA confirmed.
"Beyond that, we will concentrate our efforts on fewer simultaneous, large-scale projects, ensuring that every game we build in this space is fully set up for success," EA said.
The biggest leveraged buyout of all time

The PIF, along with Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, took EA private in a $55 billion sale that was constructed as a leveraged buyout, or LBO. This was the largest LBO ever, not just in gaming, but in the history of all business. Since the acquisition was "leveraged," that means it comes with debt, and a lot of it, so many expected EA to make major cuts to help service that debt.

Prior to the deal closing, Piers Harding-Rolls of Ampere Analysis said EA may look to “cut excess spending and rationalize the company’s workforce” to help bring in more money to address the debt. A report from Financial Times said EA might look to further bolster AI tools and technologies to help cut development costs and drive profitability.

Mat Piscatella of Circana told GI.biz that the companies being acquired in LBOs rarely fare well. “Leveraged buyouts have a certain history that generally hasn’t been great for the acquired companies,” he said.

content.v: Rayman Legends Retold is almost here, and as you'd expect from this remake, it's a pretty noticeable graphical glow-up of Rayman Legends and it includes a very French outfit for you to dress the phantom-limbed hero and his partner Barbara up in. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 fans, this is where you do the Leonardo DiCaprio pointing meme.

Even though Ubisoft doesn't mention Sandfall Interactive or Expedition 33 by name, it did confirm that the new baguette outfits are "a playful nod to a fellow game" created in Montpellier. "Conceived as a tribute from one French studio to another, these costumes celebrate the creativity, passion, and unmistakably French touch that continue to make the country's video game industry shine on the global stage," Ubisoft said in a press release. Sandfall Interactive is also headquartered in Montpellier.

The friendly homage is no doubt a tribute to Sandfall Interactive and its award-winning debut game, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. The Expedition 33 outfit features a white shirt with black pinstripes, black pants with black suspenders, a red beret, and a baguette kept inside a red-and-white plaid cloth, making it as Gallic as Groundskeeper Willie's introduction to the beautiful French language. Unlocking the outfit for each character in the hit RPG isn't easy, as players must defeat secret mime mini-bosses around the map.

The look isn't unique to either game, as the ensemble draws on 19th-century naval uniforms, Basque headwear, and "Onion Johnny" door-to-door traders. Over time, those fashion elements became synonymous with France, becoming a symbol of French elegance and casual style that artists like Pablo Picasso and fashion icon Jean Paul Gaultier adopted. You've probably also spotted people wearing these costumes at conventions, as Expedition 33's baguette outfits make for an easy, low-cost, and comfortable cosplay.

Ubisoft says the baguette costumes will be available to all players at launch, when the game launches for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch 2 on December 3. It's the second big remake from Ubisoft this year , following the release of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced in July.

items.title: WoW Forever Beta Extended to Friday, Name Reservations Go Live Tuesday
items.summary: The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other beta, it has to come t

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/19/forever-1789805930640.png

The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other, it has to come to an end as the full launch approaches. Thankfully, Blizzard has extended the beta by a couple of days.

WoW Forever's beta was supposed to end yesterday, October 20, but Blizzard announced on X/Twitter that it would be extending the experience by three days. Now the beta will end on October 23 at 10am PT / 1pm ET. After it ends, Blizzard will open name reservations on October 27, which will let you reserve names for three different characters – just make sure they don't break the rules.

It's easy to forget that WoW Forever isn't just out already. Since the beta went live in September, people have been playing it constantly, and just among people playing the beta, there have already been a million characters made. Blizzard devs have even come out and said they were surprised by how many people flocked to the temporary test version of the Classic+ game mode.
Once the full game comes out on November 4, all you'll need to play WoW: Forever is an active subscription or a friend code (though that will just be temporary), so it'll likely be even more popular.

Fans have loved how true the content in the beta so far has stayed to the spirit of the early days of World of Warcraft. Blizzard has made it a point to avoid adding some modern quality-of-life improvements like shared tagging in order to maintain that classic feel. But, rather than strictly avoiding adding anything that was added after WoW's expansions started coming out, Blizzard has included content like the beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' quest that takes place in Mulgore.

There have been controversies, too, of course – it wouldn't be WoW without them. Blizzard has had to crack down hard on gold selling , and the company has also been strict with character names . We've even seen people griefing other players by putting down campfires where new players spawn so they die before the intro cinematic finishes.
If you haven't had a chance to dive into the beta yet, you still have a couple days to do so. But keep in mind that any progress you make will be deleted when the game launches in a couple of weeks.

items.title: Another Day, Another Pokemon Card Heist Worth Nearly $1 Million

content.v: I guess someone's gotta collect 'em all, and it appears that thieves are doing just that, as yet another high-stakes burglary in Southern California has resulted in just about $1 million worth of Pokemon cards being stolen from a FedEx truck.

According to a report by The New York Times' sports journalism department, The Athletic (via ABC News ), a FedEx truck parked near the authenticating and grading business known as the Professional Sports Authenticator in Santa Ana, California, was robbed on October 13. The Santa Ana Police Department said in a statement to ABC News that hundreds of cards were stolen, with the robbery estimated at a value of $963,000.

"The pallets contained various trading cards, including, but not limited to, sports cards and Pokemon cards," the Santa Ana Police Department said in a statement. "However, the exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined."

According to the Santa Ana Police Department, the thieves broke into the FedEx truck, stole two full pallets of cards, and tore through a third pallet for even more packaged goodies--all of which belonged to collectors from across the country who submitted their cards to the Professional Sports Authenticator to be authenticated and graded for collecting or reselling purposes.

Collectors, the parent company of the Professional Sports Authenticator, told ABC News that in the wake of the theft, it has deactivated the certificates for the missing cards and notified its other businesses in its marketplace to "be on the lookout" for the cards in case they turn up.

"We are aware of a theft involving a third-party shipping vehicle carrying PSA-graded items," the company said. "We are working closely with law enforcement and the carrier as the investigation continues. Our customer service team has contacted affected customers directly and is arranging compensation based on fair market value. We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more than a financial asset."
FedEx is also aware of the burglary, telling ABC News that it's cooperating with police.

"The security of our customers' shipments is a top priority, and we are working with local law enforcement in their investigation," the corporation said. "Further questions should be referred to local investigators."

This seems to be a regular occurrence these days : people stealing tens of thousands of dollars worth of Pokemon cards , sometimes at gunpoint . What was once a fun hobby has become quite fraught as people battle each other to get their hands on cards. I don't know what happened because it wasn't like this 30 years ago , but soon, you may need a face just to buy Pokemon cards . Yikes.

items.title: Nvidia Just Tackled One Of PC Gaming’s Biggest Headaches: Shader Compilation
items.summary: One of the most annoying things about PC games is how long they can take to start, thanks to the traditional s

content.v: One of the most annoying things about PC games is how long they can take to start, thanks to the traditional shader compilation a game goes through after installation or after getting new drivers. The silver bullet to this might be Microsoft's Advanced Shader Delivery, which was used in Gears of War: E-Day to drastically cut down on its initial launch, and Nvidia graphics card owners can also take advantage of this technology starting today with the release of the version 621.01 drivers. AMD has featured this technology for a while now, but with Nvidia included, ASD will be open to the vast majority of the PC gaming community.

Available for Nvidia RTX and RTX Spark graphics cards, ASD reduces shader compilation times by downloading precompiled shaders. For now, only two games support ASD--the new Gears of War prequel and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Combined with Nvidia's Automatic Shader Compilation, which is designed to prevent shaders from needing to be recompiled after you install new drivers, this should make for a pretty seamless approach to installing a game and playing it right away, something which console owners have enjoyed for years. This is down to consoles only having one configuration, whereeas PCs come in multiple configurations, thus requiring shader compilation to set a game up on that platform.

In my own testing, ASD proved to be very quick on both my desktop PC and my Asus ROG Ally X. After installing Gears of War: E-Day, I could start the game in under a minute on either platform, a marked improvement compared to how some games asked me to wait around 10-15 minutes so that they could get their shader ducks in a row. ASD works with multiple hardware configurations, including devices powered by AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm, although results may vary between systems.
On the console side, Sony recently announced Quick Spectral Super Resolution for base PS5 consoles, and AMD has announced that FSR 4.1 is coming to Xbox Series X|S in the future.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/star-wars-battlefront-2-1792604260456.jpg
EA has confirmed that DICE and Respawn are working on a new project together, adding more fuel to rumors about Star Wars: Battlefront 3 .

As part of a larger letter about the future of EA, the publisher confirmed that it is working on new Battlefield games. It also noted that in addition to Battlefield, DICE and Respawn are working together on a "future project" that they hope will unlock growth in their shooter portfolio. This follows rumors from earlier this week that the two companies are working together to make Star Wars: Battlefront 3.

"In addition to our future Battlefield titles, we’ll be bringing together our Respawn and DICE studios to collaborate on a future project that will help us achieve that ambition," said EA. "We can’t wait to share more when the time comes."

Variety also corroborated the Battlefront 3 rumors via sources, though nothing was shared on what the game will look like or when it might release. Other rumors recently suggested that Bungie was in the mix to work on Battlefront 3 or perhaps another project in the Star Wars universe, though nothing has been confirmed on that front. Star Wars: Battlefront 3 has been one of the most demanded titles over the last decade.

DICE's second crack at the Star Wars shooter franchise was controversial at launch due to issues with its monetization strategy , but the game itself was praised up and down by fans. It has remained a respected title among Star Wars lovers, and they've frequently rallied together to demand a sequel . Now, it seems like it will happen, though this time with the assistance of Respawn.

The Titanfall and Apex Legends studio has its own experience working on Star Wars through the Jedi games and the recently-released Star Wars Zero Company. Respawn also worked on a canceled Star Wars shooter, rumored to be a Mandalorian game, leaving fans to wonder what could've been. Only time will tell what this new Respawn and DICE game really is, but if it's Battlefront 3, it has serious potential to be something special.

This news came alongside some doom and gloom. EA confirmed that it was canceling the next Mass Effect and shutting down veteran RPG studio BioWare . The news comes after about a decade of commercial and critical misfires from the studio with games like Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard.

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever will see players battling to become an ogre arena champion once more, this time in the new Riverglades zone.

Forever's launch is just a few weeks away on November 4, and every day it seems like Blizzard reveals new information about the game. In a new video titled "Your Leveling Journey Past 30," Blizzard goes into more detail about what to expect from the game's all-new Riverglades zone, diving into its Warcraft 2 lore roots and what players can expect to find there. The contested zone is divided up by multiple different factions, with the Brotherhood of the Horse representing the Alliance and the Boulder Rock ogre clan representing the Horde.

Blizzard makes a point to call out a new ogre arena in the trailer, deep within Boulder Rock territory. The Bloodmasters Ring is "a fighting ring where players will prove their strength against the ogres' best brawlers," Blizzard says in the trailer.

That will likely sound awfully familiar to anyone who has played WoW in the last 20 years, as it's reminiscent of the iconic Ring of Blood quest chain from the game's first expansion, The Burning Crusade. It's one of TBC's most memorable quests, as players needed to put together a full group of players in Nagrand to battle boss after boss, eventually rising up the ranks to become champion. The chain also granted some great rewards that many players used early on in TBCs endgame.

It's a tradition that has continued in nearly every expansion since, with a similar quest chain, the Amphitheater of Anguish, in Wrath of the Lich King and again with Cataclysm's Crucible of Carnage. The Ring of Blood itself even made a second appearance during the game's Warlords of Draenor expansion.

What kind of rewards players can expect from the Ring of Blood is still unknown, but WoW Classic is certainly no stranger to having quests grant significant and powerful rewards. Who knows? Maybe the Ring of Blood's original ringmasters, Gurgthock and Wodin, will even make an appearance.

Blizzard additionally dropped new details about what players can expect from WoW: Forever's endgame raids. Like in WoW Classic, players will need to attune themselves for Onyxia's Lair and obtain the Drakefire Amulet. Blizzard additionally warns players will want to bring some fire resistance gear for the occasion. As for the game's two new raids at launch, the eight-boss Barrow Deeps raid will have multiple entrances in zones like Mount Hyjal, Winterspring, and Blackmaw Hold, while the massive Hyjal Summit raid will have 13 bosses to defeat.

WoW: Forever is still seeing major changes two weeks before launch, with Blizzard recently changing the math on what race to play with a huge racial-ability overhaul. In an interview with GameSpot, Blizzard gave a glimpse into what WoW: Forever's future will look like and how it's approaching the MMOs endgame.

items.title: RIP BioWare：EA 关闭了传奇 RPG 开发商
items.summary: Bloomberg also reports that EA is cutting "around 400 jobs" across the company.

content.v: BioWare is closing, and the next Mass Effect game is cancelled.

The legendary RPG studio was founded in 1995 by doctors Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, and was responsible for a number of classics, including the original Baldur's Gate games , Neverwinter Nights, Jade Empire, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and more recently, the Dragon Age and Mass Effect series.
https://t.co/TicSujMWps October 21, 2026

"What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember," said the studio in a statement published on social media. "These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own."

After establishing itself in the PC gaming canon in the '90s and early 2000s, BioWare was acquired by Electronic Arts in 2007, and became a mainstream RPG powerhouse with the release of the Mass Effect trilogy and first Dragon Age games.

A 2017 follow-up to the Mass Effect trilogy, Andromeda, wasn't as well-received as the originals, and the studio's 2019 detour into live service shooters, Anthem, failed to catch on. Anthem is widely considered one of the great management blunders of the live service gold rush, and its servers were finally shut down for good earlier this year.
BioWare's most recent game, 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard , also "underperformed," according to EA.

Last year, it was announced that EA would be acquired by a consortium made up of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, the latter of which is owned by Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US president Donald Trump. The acquisition was finalized this August.

When the deal was announced, some employees and outside observers were not confident that BioWare would have a future following the acquisition, with one employee saying last year that it felt like "a matter of time" before the axe fell.

The next Mass Effect game was first teased in 2020, and was expected to bring back characters from the original trilogy. In 2025, BioWare said that "a core team at BioWare" was working on the game after layoffs at the studio.
Alongside the BioWare closure, EA is laying off around 400 people across the company, according to Bloomberg .

In a letter shared with employees and published on EA's website, the company said that "saying no to some things we're passionate about allows us to focus our teams and resources so we give our biggest opportunities everything they need to succeed."
The letter was signed by EA chief studios officer Cam Weber, who until recently headed up EA Sports, and EA COO David Tinson.

content.v: I don't send my Pokémon cards off to PSA to get graded. I'm too emotionally attached to my cards to ever sell them, so paying the hefty fee for grading doesn't really make sense for me, plus I'm a naturally anxious person. So when I heard the latest news of almost $1 million worth of TCG being stolen right outside PSA's headquarters my position was cemented.

Police in Santa Ana, California have confirmed the theft of an estimated $963,000 worth of TCG after several card collectors were notified that a truck carrying their collections had been burglarised back in mid-October.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YfbrLzatbVa8eehzF9cDDN-1920-80.png

"The pallets contained various trading cards, including, but not limited to, sports cards and Pokémon cards," the SAPD explained to The Athletic . "The exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined, pending further investigation. The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information regarding this incident is encouraged to contact the Santa Ana Police Department."

But what exactly happened, and how did two pallets holding around 100 packages get stolen? Well, according to reports a FedEx driver left their truck unattended outside PSA's Santa Ana office for around 60 to 90 minutes. This left enough time for the thieves to break off the lock to the truck and make away with all the packages.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Q9gwogWHYq9tmbEBJiL6fN-1920-80.png
FedEx released a statement to ABC7 reassuring customers that "the security of our customers' shipments is a top priority, and we are working with local law enforcement in their investigation."

PSA has also confirmed in a statement to IGN that it has promised to refund customers affected. It will hand them out "based on fair market value up to the maximum insured value" of the cards and has deactivated the certificates of all the stolen goods.

This is another sad incident in an increasingly long line of TCG thievery. Just a few months ago two men pleaded guilty to stealing over £71,000 worth of Pokémon TCG, and TCG shops have seen an increase in burglaries over the past few years as card prices go up. With no sign of it getting better I feel as if the only fix is for The Pokémon Company to flood the market, devaluing cards, and thereby removing the incentive to resell. Because let's be honest, a piece of cardboard shouldn't be selling for $70,000.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/20/pokemon-tcg-pristmatic-evolutions-elite-trainer-box-cover-1792501102180.jpg

In a world where market price has become the new MSRP for the Pokémon Trading Card Game , you can now score one of its rarest modern ETBs — Prismatic Evolutions — for only $49.99 at Best Buy , thanks to the retailer’s new invite-only listing.

Amazon’s invite-only listings for Pokémon TCG Elite Trainer Boxes and bundles have been one of the best ways to score trading cards at MSRP without having to check multiple in-person retail stores or trying to beat scalper-bots during online drops. However, their now-huge popularity has made the odds of getting one of those said invites a ‘once in a blue moon’ sort of opportunity these days.

Seeing that obvious growing issue in the retailer market, that’s likely why Best Buy has been launching sales events like this itself. Instead of paying around $130.50 for a Prismatic Evolutions Elite Trainer Box (its current market price on TCGplayer ), you can pay around 62% less if you’re lucky enough.
Said luck is still the most important factor of all here, though, as that essentially determines if you’ll be able to get one of these Pokémon ETBs for yourself.
First, you’ll need a Best Buy account, and you’ll need to be signed in as you select the “Ask for an invite” button on the page.

In the same way as Amazon’s Pokémon invites go out, your invite request will be kept on Best Buy’s system to be in consideration for the next (or future) stock drops the retailer gets for this particular ETB — before randomly selecting who amongst those requesters actually get an invite.

If you do get selected, of which you’ll be notified by email, you’ll have 24 hours to purchase your Prismatic Evolutions ETB before said invite expires. In light of that fairly narrow window, that’s also why Best Buy advises you to download and use the Best Buy app as well, so you can get real-time alert notifications, as well.

Whilst this all means requesting an invite doesn’t guarantee you’ll get selected this time, you’ll at least stay on the list for any future restocks, too, so you don’t need to request one again each time.

As for what you can get when you finally get an invite, the standard Prismatic Evolutions Elite Trainer Box includes nine Prismatic Evolutions booster packs, an exclusive full-art foil Eevee promo card, 65 Eevee-themed sleeves, 45 Energy cards, dice, condition markers, a player's guide, and a collector's storage box.

items.title: GTA 6 将包含许多小细节，例如 Red Dead 的动态马睾丸物理
items.summary: New details about Rockstar's GTA 6 continue to come to light ahead of the highly anticipated crime game's rele

content.v: New details about Rockstar's GTA 6 continue to come to light ahead of the highly anticipated crime game's release in November. Reporter Jason Schreier published a video recently in which he discussed some of the new things about GTA 6 that he learned when interviewing Rockstar, including how the game will feature the next evolution of fine details like the horse testicle system in Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption II, along with information about the game's roads and "dark" years of development on the project.

One of the details is that GTA 6's roads are narrower, generally, than what GTA 5 had--and that was on purpose. The roads are "significantly" narrower, Schreier said that Rockstar's Aaron Garbut told him, and players will have denser traffic scenarios to deal with. Anyone who's played GTA 5 knows that some of the roads are wide open, allowing players to zip around like an action movie.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/GTA_5c11e2.jpg?w=636

Players can do that in GTA 6 as well, but Schreier said Rockstar told him that the team planned on narrower roads from the onset of development, and this caused "ripple effects" for the game overall. "All these things come back to bite you later," Garbut said, referring to how narrower roads meant that the team had to create more buildings and generally more elements to accomodate this.

Also in the video, Schreier said Rockstar faced "dark" times between 2019-2022 due to not only COVID, but also because that was when Rockstar was determing how realistic they wanted to make GTA 6. Finding the balance between realism and the arcade-style fun that GTA is known for was a key point of discussion at Rockstar around this time, and it caused some tension internally, Schreier said.

Around this time, Rockstar's Rob Nelson told Schreier that the studio was thinking about making GTA 6's weapon system more realistic and only allowing players to hold a set number of weapons in their arsenal. Rockstar spent "months if not years" experimenting with different designs for a new system to evolve the traditional weapon wheel, or get rid of it entirely. However, after all that time, Rockstar decided to stick with the familiar weapon-wheel setup.

Another interesting fact from the video is that, according to Garbut, there is "no one person that has this whole thing in their head," referring to GTA 6 itself. Schreier said individual developers working on GTA 6 are given a level of autonomy that allows them to add small details that other colleagues might be totally unaware of.

Schreier pointed out how one of the granular details in Red Dead Redemption II was how your horse's testicles would shrink or expand based on the weather. That was never something that was on a "features list" for the game or an idea that a director asked for. Instead, someone, or a team of people, came up with this on their own and put it in the game. Schreier said GTA 6 will have its own version of this, with individual developers or teams inserting granular details that might otherwise go unnoticed.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's expected to be a huge hit commercially, and it's already tracking ahead of all the other big AAA games of recent times.

content.v: Now this is a marketing campaign I can get behind: It looks very much like Rockstar is teaming up with Florida-based brewery Tripping Animals Brewing to bring a trio of Grand Theft Auto 6 -themed beers into the real world. That's right— Pißwasser is finally real.

The discovery was made by Grand Theft Auto site GTAVice.net , which found labels for Pißwasser, Patriot, and No Mames Vice City—a re-branding of Tripping Animals' No Mames Lager—in the US Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau database .

Sure enough, they're in there, although I had to use Hopgrail to dig up the labels: The No Mames Vice City label was approved on October 9, while the Pißwasser and Patriot labels followed on October 15.
So what's in the cans?
NO MAMES VICE CITY
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/i5n2Xb7YXeckQ9ahaKb29P-1920-80.jpg

This looks to be a re-brand of Tripping Animals' No Mames beer, so here's what the brewery's website has to say about it: "Bright gold and effortlessly crisp, No Mames blends flaked corn and traditional malts for a smooth, dry lager with subtle floral hops and a hint of sweetness. Clean, crushable, and brewed for easy drinking, anytime."
Patriot and Pißwasser are not yet on the Tripping Animals site, so for those we will go with what we can pull from the TTB database, which frankly isn't much:
PATRIOT BEER
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/BmP3T33T5BJMPnDLnuoj5P-1920-80.jpg
4.2% ABV American lager

A very American lager, the GTA Fandom Wiki says Patriot Beer is possibly inspired by Sam Adams, although it notes that the color scheme of the label is more akin to PBR. Personally I think it's more likely a prescient take on Real American Beer , which is basically a GTA-style parody beer, except it's real. Real American .
PIßWASSER
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pDrMBtgVB8bB9ewUF53LCP-1920-80.jpg
4.2% ABV lager

The king of GTA beers, Pißwasser is of course a pilsner, it says so right on the label. Now, your local beer nerd is probably leaning forward in his chair to tell you that pilsner is a type of lager, but my local beer nerd, who is me, says that yes, that is technically correct, but it's important to be specific about these things. Otherwise you get people telling you that Rolling Rock and Warsteiner are basically the same, and next thing you know you're in a fistfight with Bill from your grade 10 geography class and then somebody calls the cops and you end up running through people's back yards and tripping over shit and ripping your pants, and nobody gets any beer. Who needs that kind of chaos?

Anyway, none of these brews are confirmed as actually happening at this point, although given their appearances in the TTB database, not to mention Rockstar's largesse with its rental of basically the entire state of Florida to promote GTA 6, it's all but certainly real. It's also an obvious fit, particularly given the meta-popularity of GTA's in-game beer brands.

The bigger question for me is, how do I get some? Promo beers tend not to be great, but No Mames holds a very respectable 85 rating on Beeradvocate , and Tripping Animals seems quite well regarded overall. And let's not forget the all-important bottom line here: it's beer .

Sadly for me (and anyone else not living in Florida who'd like to score a few cans) Tripping Animals distribution appears quite limited: The brewery's website indicates its beers are only available in and around—you guessed it—Miami. Ah well.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to launch on consoles on November 19. I would expect the GTA beers to show up by then too.
