items.title: GTA 6 Might Give America A Very Expensive Sick Day
items.summary: Everyone wants to play Rockstar Games' upcoming heist-'em-up Grand Theft Auto 6 --so much so that some 1.5 mil

content.v: Everyone wants to play Rockstar Games' upcoming heist-'em-up Grand Theft Auto 6 --so much so that some 1.5 million Americans are projected to call in sick to work on November 19 to play the game, which an economics professor estimates will set the country back roughly $1 billion.

According to an International Business Times report , economics professor José García Montalvo projected that the 1.5 million workers planning to play hooky to traipse around Leonida next month could cost America a boatload of money. If each worker has an annual salary of $70,000, Montalvo suggests that the math works out to $1 billion, with GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive estimated to make that same amount on November 19.

That's the catch. The American economy isn't necessarily losing money; the bills are just changing hands, from the pockets of the country writ large to those of one multi-billion-dollar corporation. I'm sure you know the saying: The rich get richer.
It's worth noting, though, that this isn't an official forecast. Rather, Montalvo's estimation is a mere academic projection.

However, the phenomenon has a precedent in the hype surrounding Grand Theft Auto 5 's launch in September 2013, when an IGN poll found that 46% of its nearly 11,000 respondents planned to take the day off work as a holiday for "GTA flu." That self-selected poll measured readers' intentions, not actual workplace absences across US cities like Los Angeles and New York. Still, it's evidence that Rockstar Games' games are a moment in pop culture, creating a monoculture we haven't had in a minute.

And some people are very serious about taking time off to play the game. Bud Burruss, a streamer and father of three, told the Wall Street Journal in September that he plans to take a five-day vacation. Others took to social media to share similar sentiments, with some couples drafting contracts and labeling the act of playing the game as "cheating." Even the military is offering some days off for its soldiers at Fort Stewart, Georgia, to play GTA 6, so you know the "GTA flu" is real.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/screenshot-2026-10-21-165756-1792598292233.png
CD Projekt has revealed what to expect from the Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 update, which ties in with the release of Netflix anime Edgerunners 2 .

Edgerunners content includes a new side quest called Clampdown, which is set before the events of Edgerunners 2 ( CD Projekt recently confirmed that Edgerunners 2 is set in 2078 , just one year after the game itself). During this quest you’ll get a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King from Season 2. There’s also a new radio station that has tracks from the Edgerunners series.

But there’s plenty more coming with 2.5 unrelated to Edgerunners, including more side quests. The Welcome to Paradise! side quest takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night, the founder of Night City itself. There’s also a new side quest that acts as an extension of Fool on the Hill, which includes new tarot cards.

Meanwhile, 2.5 lets you customize your hand cyberware, which will let you give your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System implants a new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

Perhaps the most significant addition with 2.5 is the new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree, which lets you dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category for the first time. The hope is that the perk will enable an entirely new playstyle, and I’m sure fans will get a kick out of trying it out.

Elsewhere, there’s cross-platform mod support on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X and S, and various quality-of-life improvements, such as saves in the “Load Game” menu grouped by separate playthroughs, and, finally, an FOV (Field Of View) slider on consoles.

On the tech side of things, there’s support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model, and various performance improvements.

Overall, 2.5 is a welcome surprise for Cyberpunk 2077, after CD Projekt had indicated it had no plans for further DLC for the hugely successful game. Of course, The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion 12 years after launch, so perhaps CD Projekt will return later on with a new expansion for Cyberpunk 2077. For now, though, 2.5 is sure to spark a return to Night City for lapsed players, and give fans of Edgerunners a push to jump in if they haven’t already.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2023/08/24/ste-1692892641332.png

Magic: The Gathering: Star Trek is the card game's final frontier of 2026, and while Wizards of the Coast revealed quite a few of the cards yesterday, IGN today has seven cards we can exclusively reveal ahead of the November 13 release date.

Just like the Marvel Superheroes set that came out earlier this year, Magic: The Gathering Star Trek has cards from pretty much every era of the show's history. Even the small selection of cards we have here covers everything from the original series to Deep Space 9 and Lower Decks.
MTG Star Trek Exclusive Card Reveals
We're revealing seven exclusive Magic: The Gathering Star Trek cards:

The star of the show is a common artifact called 'Tea, Earl Grey, Hot.' Really, the reason why this card is noteworthy is because of the reference to Captain Picard's hot beverage of choice, but in the right deck, it could do some work. It's simply a 2 mana artifact with the 'Food' subtype, which automatically makes it useful in some decks.

But unlike the Food Tokens we've all made hundreds of, this one nets you a card when it enters. When you sacrifice it, you can either gain 3 life like any other Food Token, or you can have it deal 2 damage to an opponent. Finally, I can just throw tea in someone's face.

The more mechanically interesting card is Mirror Universe Intrusion. It's a sorcery for a colorless, a blue and a black, that lets you create a copy of a creature an opponent controls, only it has menace. That's a flavor win, but something that you can do with countless other cards.

However, if you pay the kicker of 4 colorless, a blue and a black, you instead copy all of your opponent's creatures, and give them all menace. At nine mana, it's quite an investment, but a good way to essentially steal an opponent's board.
Mirror Universe Intrusion also has a couple of 'booster fun' treatments, with a borderless version and the new showcase treatment that loos like it came right out of a Star Trek box set.

Dahar Master is a 4-mana 4/3 at common, and with its ability to sacrifice a nonland permanant to shock any target, should be useful at your prerelease. But it's kind of one of those cards that's going to end up populating a bulk box the day after you open it in a pack.

Unexplored Wilds is interesting, becuase it's an effect we've seen countless times with cards like Evolving Wilds, but worse. You can tap it for a colorless mana, unlike Evolving Wilds, but if you want to sacrifice it to tutor up a basic land, you need to spend one mana to do it, which is bad. Just like Dahar Master, this will probably be useful in draft to help you color fix, but it's going to end up in your bulk box the moment you get home.

This new Star Trek set is shaping up to at least be the most interesting Universes Beyond set of the year so far, and I am interested to see how some of the artifact strategies play out across different formats. This set is also getting previewed after Wizards of the Coast revealed Darkhold Destiny at an NYCC panel , which takes a Universes Beyond property and creates a wholly original story.
